title: Stealth rollout toggle checklist and 48h steward calendar (feature-toggle first)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, actionable checklist for small-footprint (stealth) rollouts that rely on server-side feature toggles. Focus: move fast, measure incremental impact, and have deterministic rollback steps. This is opinionated for low-risk infra/model-side changes and UI flags where we can do staged exposure via cohorts.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- Flip toggle to 0.5% -> observe 30m -> if stable, 5% -> 1h -> if stable, 25% -> 4h -> 100% or hold. Always keep automatic rollback triggers enabled.

Preflight (T-48h):
- Announce in #release-ops and product channel with short blurb (who/what/when/how to rollback).
- Create small Jira REL ticket with rollout steps and owner (REL-9483).
- Verify canary telemetry dashboards exist and target metrics: p99 latency, cpu/gpu util, error-rate, token-cost delta, model-quality sniffers.
- Confirm feature toggle implementation (server flag name, default, kill-switch).
- Smoke test plan: 10 synthetic requests covering edge cases. Add to smoke-runbook.
- Billing watch: set sampling on cost metrics.
- Assign 48h steward shifts (see calendar below).

T-1h / Preflip checklist:
- Re-run smoke tests.
- Ensure rollback playbook pinned in channel.
- Quiet-window: avoid other releases +/-2h if possible. (Notes: not always possible for emergent patches).
- TTL on toggle staging group set (auto-revert if steward unresponsive).

Flip plan (operational steps):
- Step 0: Ensure traffic can be segmented by cohort (region / user-tier / random sampling).
- Step 1 (0.5%): apply toggle, wait 30m, surface p95/p99 and error traces.
- Step 2 (5%): increase, wait 1h, run synthetic batch and quick eval on key prompt-set.
- Step 3 (25%): increase, wait 4h, check business metrics and fuzzy regressions.
- Step 4 (drift to 100% OR hold): release teams decide (manual gates).

Automatic rollback triggers (these are enforced in the orchestrator):
- 5x baseline error rate within 15m window.
- p99 latency increase > 300ms absolute for ML endpoints OR > 2x baseline relative.
- Token cost per request > 1.5x baseline sustained for 30m.
- Model quality sentinel: failing > 3/5 golden prompts on rerun.

Manual rollback matrices: (who can push / why)
- Steward (primary): immediate rollback for quick fixes.
- Service Owner (backend/model): rollback + postmortem if triggered by model quality or infra degradation.
- Eng Oncall (SRE): emergency rollback for cascading infra issues.

48h steward calendar (compact shifts)
Day 0 (release day):
- 08:00 IST — preflight check (owner Lena).
- 09:30 IST — toggle 0.5% (steward Marco).
- 10:00 IST — first telemetry review (Marco).
- 11:30 IST — toggle to 5% (Aisha).
- 12:30 IST — synthetic eval batch (Aisha + Tom).
- 16:30 IST — toggle 25% (Lena).
- 20:00 IST — make hold vs full decision; if go, plan final ramp overnight.

Day 1 (stabilization):
- 00:00 IST — midnight check (Tom).
- 08:00 IST — recap + signals review (Lena).
- 12:00 IST — extended 24h post-release snapshot (product + analytics).
- 24:00 IST — formal stabilization check and either fully flip or schedule staged unwind.

Notes to steward rotations: keep handoff notes brief: outstanding anomalies, traces to watch, active Jira links, and 'accepted risk' items. If steward misses 15m check, auto reverts.

Telemetry dashboard checklist (must be visible in launch channel):
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route (split charged vs free).
- Error rate by code (5xx, 429, model-incoherent flagged).
- Infrastructure: GPU memory pressure, host load, queue lengths.
- Business signals: embed request volume, chat sessions started, top-of-funnel conversion (if affected).
- Cost sampling: tokens per session and cost delta.

Release notes (draft snippet to paste into release email/confluence):
- Feature: Toggle-enable short-form production rollout for model XYZ change (quantization kernel update).
- Why: Reduces per-token cost without changing API contract; staged rollout to validate user-facing quality.
- Rollout plan: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> decision to 100% over ~48 hours.
- Rollback criteria: automatic triggers for latency/error/cost/quality described in playbook.
- Contacts: Lena Thompson (owner), Marco Ruiz (steward), Eng oncall.

Post-release tasks (T+48–72h):
- Collect signal snapshots and attach to Jira.
- Author a short postmortem if any trigger fired.
- Validate A/B cohorts for long-term quality metrics (7-day window).
- Follow-up: consider permanent toggle removal or re-architect if needed.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether to include region-specific throttles for APAC (some infra quirks). (TODO: @Tom to verify).
- Define golden prompt-set for model-quality sentinels (partial list attached in linked artifacts).
- Should we wire a quiet-mode that throttles model size for heavy prompts? (note: cost tradeoffs).

Scratch / quick commands to run during release:
- smoke run: ./scripts/smoke-run.sh --suite stealth-48h
- toggle CLI: infractl feature-toggle set --name=toggle_xyz --pct=0.5 --owner=lena
- rollback: infractl feature-toggle set --name=toggle_xyz --pct=0 --reason="rollback by stewardship"

Quick comm blurb (paste into Slack):
"Rolling out toggle_xyz today (Lena). Plan: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% over 48h with automatic rollback. Steward schedule posted. Ping @release-ops or @lena if you see regressions. Jira REL-9483."

Notes-to-self style: keep the release small if product-facing; model changes are riskier. If we see model-quality drift early, prefer rollback and A/B offline evals rather than incremental ramp.

Revision history:
- 2027-03-02 Lena: initial draft and calendar.
- 2027-03-04 Marco: added automatic rollback triggers and commands.

END.
